info.bio:
Eddie Cochran (Albert Lea (Minnesota), 3 de octubre de 1938 - Chippenham, Wiltshire (Inglaterra), 17 de abril de 1960) fue un músico de rockabilly estadounidense. Su nombre real era Edward Ray Cochrane.

Eddie Cochran nació y creció en Albert Lea, Minnesota. Empezó su carrera musical en 1955 con un amigo llamado Hank Cochran,que sería más tarde un letrista de música country. A pesar del apellido común, no existía entre ellos ningún lazo de parentesco.

scenes.name: Rock'n'roll
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Fusión de rhythm'n'blues y country, con mucho más peso del primero. Chuck Berry inventa en 1955 el rock'n'roll tal como se conocerá durante cincuenta años (la guitarra como instrumento protagonista, canciones propias que hablan a los adolescentes); Bo Diddley aporta el ritmo «hambone», Little Richard y Esquerita el histerismo y el maquillaje (el primer «decadence-rock»), Jerry Lee Lewis el piano feroz y Sun Records el rockabilly. Elvis Presley es, para Scaruffi, «la primera gran estafa del rock'n'roll». Buddy Holly y Eddie Cochran abren otra vía; en paralelo nacen el soul (Ray Charles), la exótica (Martin Denny, Esquivel), la música electrónica de cinta y, en Gran Bretaña, el skiffle.

scenes.name: Antes del diluvio
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La «edad oscura» del rock'n'roll: los rebeldes son sustituidos por ídolos adolescentes educados y el Brill Building devuelve el poder a los compositores profesionales. Pero en esos años se incuban la revolución futura: la guitarra fuzz de Link Wray, los bailes de moda (el twist), el rock instrumental de guitarras (Duane Eddy, Ventures, Shadows), el calipso y el primer ska, el doo-wop más inventivo (Coasters, Drifters, Five Royales), el nacimiento del soul (Sam Cooke, Ray Charles, Motown, Stax), el estudio como instrumento de Joe Meek y el surf de los Beach Boys y del «muro de sonido» de Phil Spector.

podcast.title: Appearance in "Go Johnny Go" Film
podcast.body: Eddie Cochran was among the prominent musicians who appeared in the Alan Freed film "Go Johnny Go," a movie that also showcased Richie Valens. "Valens appeared in the Alan Fried film Go Johnny Go, which featured Chuck Berry, Eddie Cochran, The Flamingos, and Jackie Wilson."

podcast.title: Death and Impact on Derry Weaver
podcast.body: Derry Weaver was living at the Sheely Residence when he received the phone call announcing Eddie Cochran's death and Sharon Sheely's hospitalization. This event deeply haunted Weaver for the rest of his life. "Weaver was actually living it the Shealy Residence, when they received the phone call saying that Eddie had died and Shaman was in hospital, and it haunted him deeply for the rest of his life."

podcast.title: Elvis Impersonator
podcast.body: Eddie Cochran impersonated Elvis Presley on The Holly Twins' song "I Want Elvis for Christmas." "He'd started out as a songwriter, working with his friend Bobby Damien on songs like I Want Elvis for Christmas, which had been recorded by the Holly Twins with Eddie Cochrane impersonating Elvis."

podcast.title: Friendship and Missed Tour (Year not specified)
podcast.body: Eddie Cochran became fast friends with The Crickets and was scheduled to join Buddy Holly on the Winter Dance Party tour. However, he received an offer to perform on the Ed Sullivan Show, which clashed with the tour dates, and so he did not participate. "Bodies friend Eddie Cochran was going to go on tour with them as well, but shortly before the tour started, Cochran got an offer to do the Ed Sullivan show, which would have clashed with the tour dates, and so he didn't make it."

podcast.title: Influence on The Sex Pistols
podcast.body: Eddie Cochran wrote songs about teenage boredom. These tracks were later covered by later generations of punk bands, specifically mentioning the Sex Pistols, indicating his lasting influence on rebellious youth culture. "Eddie Cochrane, who songs about teenage boredom were later covered by sedentions of the sex pistols."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Inspiration for Songwriting
podcast.body: Touring with Eddie Cochrane (and Gene Vincent), Roy Orbison observed that many artists had only one hit and struggled to find new material. This prompted Orbison to take songwriting seriously as his primary artistic pursuit to ensure a consistent supply of new songs. "He realised that they, and the other people on the bill, had one hit each. Cochrane would later have more, but still, Orbison wondered where those people's other hits were going to come from, where were they going to find their material."

podcast.title: Mentoring Derry Weaver
podcast.body: Eddie Cochran taught Derry Weaver several of the guitar licks he used, significantly influencing Weaver's playing. Cochran also played guitar on a session for Weaver produced by Jerry K-Part. "Cochran taught Weaver several of the guitar licks he used."

podcast.title: Untimely Death After Film Release
podcast.body: Eddie Cochran was featured in the 1959 film "Go Johnny Go." Tragically, he died within a little over 18 months after the film's release, making him one of several artists associated with the movie who met an early end. "within a little over 18 months after its release, Cochran was also dead."

xref.title: Filming for "The Great Rock and Roll Swindle" – Paris Trip
xref.body: Malcolm McLaren had the idea for Sid to continue as the new singer for the Sex Pistols. Sid traveled to Paris to film sequences for the movie "The Great Rock and Roll Swindle," performing Eddie Cochran songs. This trip was awful due to Sid and Malcolm's animosity and Nancy's continued drug supply. "The Sex Pistols could carry on with Sid as the new singer. So it was off to Paris in a cloud of junk to film a couple of sequences for a film that would end up being called the Great Rock and Roll Swindle."
